pairs.reasoning: Ice-cream and cold-drink sales track each other because both are pulled up by hot weather (temperatur_c), not because one drives the other. Hold temperature fixed and the shared movement largely disappears.
pairs.needed_data: temperatur_c controlled for via partial correlation (already measured in this dataset).

ruled_out.label: causal
ruled_out.why: Selling ice cream doesn't cause more cold drinks to be sold.

ruled_out.label: reverse_causal
ruled_out.why: And cold-drink sales don't drive ice-cream sales either.

ruled_out.label: selection
ruled_out.why: Both are full daily sales totals, not a filtered subset of days.

ruled_out.label: chance
ruled_out.why: The association is strong and consistent across the whole summer, not noise.

pairs.reasoning: Pool visitors and ice-cream sales rise and fall together only because hot weather (temperatur_c) drives both. Neither going swimming nor buying ice cream causes the other; once temperature is held fixed the link all but vanishes.
pairs.needed_data: temperatur_c held constant (partial correlation) — available here, so the confounder can be confirmed directly.

ruled_out.label: causal
ruled_out.why: Going to the pool doesn't make the town buy more ice cream.

ruled_out.label: reverse_causal
ruled_out.why: Buying ice cream doesn't send people to the pool.

ruled_out.label: selection
ruled_out.why: Both figures cover the whole town each day, not a hand-picked subgroup.

ruled_out.label: chance
ruled_out.why: The co-movement is very strong and repeats across the entire summer.

pairs.reasoning: The textbook spurious link: ice-cream sales and drowning accidents both spike on hot days because warm weather (temperatur_c) sends people to buy ice cream AND into the water. There is no causal arrow between them — controlling for temperature collapses the correlation.
pairs.needed_data: temperatur_c controlled for via partial correlation (already measured here).

ruled_out.label: causal
ruled_out.why: Eating ice cream obviously cannot cause drowning accidents.

ruled_out.label: reverse_causal
ruled_out.why: And drownings cannot drive ice-cream sales.

ruled_out.label: selection
ruled_out.why: Both are daily town-wide counts, not a selected sample.

ruled_out.label: chance
ruled_out.why: The seasonal pattern is far too strong and regular to be coincidence.
